sciNewtonL: A net force of 24 N acts on a 6 kg cart. What is its acceleration?
By the second law, a = F ÷ m = 24 N ÷ 6 kg = 4 m/s².
A 1200 kg car accelerates at 3 m/s². What net force acts on it?

A ball pushed with a net force of 15 N accelerates at 5 m/s². What is its mass?

A 0.5 kg ball accelerates at 8 m/s². What net force acts on it?

The first law describes inertia: objects resist changes to their motion.
A book rests on a table. By Newton's third law, the table …
pushes up on the book with an equal force
pushes up on the book with a smaller force
pushes up on the book with a larger force
exerts no force at all on the book
Third-law force pairs are always equal in size and opposite in direction.
If the net force on an object doubles and its mass stays the same, its acceleration …
Acceleration is directly proportional to net force (a = F ÷ m).
The same net force acts on an object with twice the mass. Its acceleration …
Acceleration is inversely proportional to mass, so doubling the mass halves it.
An object moving at a constant velocity has a net force that is …
By the first law, an object with no net force keeps a constant velocity.
In a sudden stop, a seatbelt is needed because …
your body keeps moving forward due to inertia
the seat pushes your body forward in a stop
gravity pulls your body forward in a stop

When a bat hits a ball, the force of the ball on the bat is …
equal in size and opposite in direction

larger, because the ball speeds up

Why don't action–reaction force pairs cancel each other out?
Forces can only cancel when they act on the same object, and third-law pairs act on two different objects.
What is the SI unit of force, equal to 1 kg·m/s²?

Two skaters push apart. A 60 kg skater pushes a 40 kg skater with 120 N. What is the 40 kg skater's acceleration?
The 40 kg skater feels 120 N, so a = 120 N ÷ 40 kg = 3 m/s².
In the same push, a 60 kg skater feels 120 N from a 40 kg skater. What is the 60 kg skater's acceleration?
By the third law the 60 kg skater also feels 120 N, so a = 120 N ÷ 60 kg = 2 m/s².
A 2 kg box is pushed right with 10 N while friction pulls left with 4 N. What is its acceleration?
The net force is 10 N − 4 N = 6 N to the right, and a = 6 N ÷ 2 kg = 3 m/s².
A heavy truck and a light car get the same net force from their engines. Which accelerates faster?
For the same force, a smaller mass gives a larger acceleration (a = F ÷ m).
When you walk forward, what force actually pushes you forward?
The ground pushing forward on your feet
Your feet pushing backward on the ground
Air pushing forward on your back
Your feet push back on the ground, and by the third law the ground pushes forward on you.
Which law best explains this? A coin on a card stays put and drops into a cup when the card is flicked away.
The coin's inertia keeps it at rest when the card is quickly removed.
Which law best explains this? An empty shopping cart is much easier to speed up than a full one.
The second law says a larger mass needs a larger force for the same acceleration.
Which law best explains this? A squid squirts water backward and shoots forward.
The squid pushes water back, so the water pushes the squid forward with an equal and opposite force.
Which law best explains this? A hockey player on skates pushes on the boards and glides away from them.
The boards push back on the player with a force equal and opposite to the player's push.
